traps.why: At 180 °C the 1° alcohol dehydrates to the alkene. The ether forms at 140 °C.
Step 1 (H₂SO₄, Δ) does nothing here: A 1° alcohol only dehydrates at ~180 °C (at 140 °C it gives the ether); plain heat is not enough.

explanation: At 140 °C a second molecule of the alcohol displaces water from the protonated alcohol (SN2): a symmetric ether. At 180 °C elimination wins.

flaws.why: Step 1 (H₂SO₄, Δ) does nothing here: A 1° alcohol only dehydrates at ~180 °C (at 140 °C it gives the ether); plain heat is not enough.
